blindSummary:
Trans visitors face serious risk here — with a directly documented trans-traveller death in police custody and a presidential decree classifying LGBTQ+ people as a national security threat. A foreign trans graduate student, a citizen of a country outside the region, died in police custody on the country's best-known tourist island in 2022 after arrest at the island's airport on his honeymoon (the family alleges a police beating; the police deny violence).

In one province, a religious legal system criminalises same-sex relations with public caning, and it applies to all persons in that province, including tourists. A new penal code effective January 2026 effectively criminalises all same-sex conduct nationally. The president classified "promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" as a national security threat alongside terrorism in October 2025 — and vigilante mob attacks on trans women escalated after this decree (10 attacks documented in a capital-satellite city between March and July 2026). Police conduct discriminatory raids on gay gatherings (75 arrested in the same city in June 2025).

BUT: the best-known tourist island is a major hub where many trans visitors enter discreetly without incident; there is no death penalty; and the custody death is disputed (police deny violence) rather than clearly documented state torture.
blindOutOfScope: Drug laws are severe (the custody death above began with a drug arrest); general terrorism/crime risks in certain regions affect all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying international newswire report (Aug 2022) covers this country's police denying violence in the death of a foreign trans graduate student in police custody on the tourist island.

The university's student newspaper (Sept 2022): the mother of the 32-year-old foreign trans man who died in custody - a foreign national studying abroad - alleges he was arrested at the tourist island's airport on drug charges, subjected to extortion (demands rising from $100,000 to $200,000), and died three days later in hospital while in police custody during his honeymoon.

Regional policy magazine (Aug 2026): the transgender community in this country faces growing repression - vigilante mobs attacking trans people as the government takes steps to codify anti-LGBT provisions.

Foreign news outlet (Aug 2026): analysis of attacks on trans women in this country after a rule deemed them a 'threat' - trans women who were previously able to appear in public have become afraid; the attacks did not appear suddenly but build on longer trends.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying international newswire report (Feb 2025) covers the province under religious law publicly caning two men for a same-sex relationship.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the new penal code in force from 2 January 2026 penalises all consensual extra-marital sex (2 years), effectively criminalising same-sex relations since marriage is unavailable to same-sex couples (complaint-based enforcement); the vague 2016 anti-pornography law has been used to target LGBTIQ people - 2025 police raids on 'gay parties' detained 56 in the capital, 75 in a capital-satellite city and 34 in a major commercial city; online LGBTIQ content blocked.

International legal-aid trust country profile: two provinces of this country - one under a religious legal system, another elsewhere - criminalise same-sex sexual activity between men and between women; national-level provisions target morality.

International human-rights organisation (June 2025): police raided a privately rented villa in a capital-satellite city described as a 'gay party', arresting 75 people (74 men, 1 woman); the organisation called the raid a flagrant violation of human rights and privacy exemplifying the hostile environment for LGBTI people in this country, and demanded release and accountability.
An international rights group (Jul 2026): documents a surge in abuse of LGBT students by authorities and institutions in this country.

International human-rights organisation report (Aug 2016) on the threat to this country's LGBT community - 70 interviews; documents the anti-LGBT cascade starting with the higher-education minister's campus ban call, the defence minister portraying LGBT activism as a danger greater than nuclear attack, and resulting legislative proposals threatening LGBT people's rights and safety.
blindTangential: The new penal code (January 2026) criminalising all same-sex conduct nationally, and a province's religious-law caning provision (applying to tourists), are direct risks for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
